name: Silvretta-Bielerhöhe & Reservoir
kurzbeschreibung: The Silvretta-Bielerhöhe at 2,037 m: Alpine pass between Tyrol and Vorarlberg with the turquoise Silvretta Reservoir facing the iconic Piz Buin (3,312 m).
beschreibung:
Overview

The awe-inspiring Silvretta-Bielerhöhe sits at an alpine mountain pass elevation of 2,037 metres, marking the border between Tyrol (Paznaun/Galtür, Landeck district) and Vorarlberg (Montafon). Surrounded by the glaciated peaks of the Silvretta range—crowned by Vorarlberg's highest summit, the majestic Piz Buin (3,312 m), and the rugged Silvrettahorn—this high plateau is one of the premier alpine destinations in the Austrian Alps. The centrepiece of the pass is the vast turquoise-tinted Silvretta Reservoir, operated by energy supplier Illwerke vkw for renewable hydroelectric generation.

Panoramic Scenery & Alpine Activities

In summer, the Bielerhöhe is reached via the world-famous toll road Silvretta High Alpine Road, winding up in 34 dramatic hairpin bends from Galtür and Partenen. Upon arriving at the pass, a vast alpine arena unfolds. Among the most popular experiences is the 2.5-hour Silvretta Reservoir Circular Trail: spanning roughly 6.5 kilometres, the wide, level path traces the shoreline and crosses both towering dam crests. In midsummer, the motor vessel MS Silvretta offers scenic boat excursions across the water—Europe's only scheduled passenger boat service operating above 2,000 metres. For mountaineers, the pass serves as the gateway to the Silvretta glaciers and high refuges like the Wiesbadener Hütte (2,443 m) and Berggasthof Piz Buin.

Visit & Getting There

The Silvretta-Bielerhöhe is open to vehicle traffic from early June until late October via the Silvretta High Alpine Road. During winter months, the road is closed to private vehicular traffic; the pass is then accessible exclusively from Partenen via the Vermunt cable car and tunnel minibuses for cross-country skiers and winter hikers. Summer road toll (2025/2026 season): private car approx. €19.50 day pass. Arriving by car: from Landeck drive through the Paznaun Valley past Ischgl and Galtür to the toll station and up to the Bielerhöhe summit. By public transit: from Landeck-Zams railway station, regional bus 260 travels via Galtür directly to the Bielerhöhe Silvrettasee terminus.

Tips

The loop trail circling the reservoir is predominantly flat and accessible for all-terrain strollers. Don't miss stopping for refreshments on the sun terraces of Berggasthof Piz Buin, enjoying Tyrolean dumplings with direct views of the Piz Buin glacier. Allow ample time for scenic photography stops across the dam crest.
